purpose: How a print/copy equipment dealer decides which organizations in a territory still generate enough pages to justify a placement, how the lease and per-page service offer is shaped, priced as a mechanism and disclosed in plain language, how the campaign is timed against the incumbent agreement's expiration and notice calendar, and what must be true — evidenced volume, honest total cost, acknowledged terms, verified signing authority — before a signed order is handed to the deployment team.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is a dealer, agent or branch that places multifunction devices and printers into private and public organizations under an equipment lease plus a per-page service agreement, and earns from equipment placement, the lease stream and the service annuity

the lease paper is usually assigned at funding to a third-party leasing company or a manufacturer captive finance arm, so the dealer controls the offer and the disclosure but not the credit decision, the lessor's boilerplate or the end-of-term administration

every rate, lease rate factor, page rate, buyout figure, program fund and margin percentage is deal-specific, funder-specific and time-specific; this knowledge base carries the mechanism that produces such a number and the way to verify it against a current written quote, never a figure asserted as market fact

contract, commercial-protection, public-procurement and data-protection requirements differ by jurisdiction, entity type and contract and change over time; obligation classes are named here and current rules must be verified locally with the customer's own purchasing office, compliance owner and counsel

per-account print volume is normally measurable from device meters, supply purchase history or the incumbent's invoices; where it genuinely cannot be measured, the assumption is written down, labelled as an assumption and given a true-up mechanism
exclusions: the print-volume and workflow assessment method itself — meter capture procedure, walkthrough mapping, device right-sizing arithmetic and fleet consolidation modelling belong to the fleet-assessment and deployment knowledge base

delivery, network and scan integration, driver and user setup, training, and the activation of service coverage, consumable replenishment and response terms as delivered operations — deployment knowledge base

realized per-page service margin, consumable logistics and service-cost control, meter-read collection and billing integrity, and invoice production on the installed base — lease/service economics knowledge base

management of the dealer's own installed-base renewal book: the upgrade versus extend versus return decision on accounts already owned, retention through uptime, and renewal execution — lease/service economics knowledge base (this knowledge base covers the competitive displacement of somebody else's incumbent agreement)

personalized financial, legal, tax or accounting advice, including how a customer should treat a lease on their own books or whether a specific clause is enforceable against them; obligation classes are named and the customer is referred to their own advisors

any specific interest rate, lease rate factor, page rate, buyout amount, commission percentage, dealer margin percentage or market-size figure stated as fact rather than as a mechanism to be verified per deal
consumer and household printer retail, cartridge remanufacturing and e-commerce supplies merchandising
technical repair procedure, parts diagnosis, firmware and driver engineering, and device security configuration as an engineering task
drafting, interpreting or opining on a customer's contract as legal counsel; clauses are read here operationally so a customer understands what they are signing, which is not a legal opinion

competency_questions.question: Which organizations in this territory still print enough to justify placing equipment, and what specifically generates their pages?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRINT_VOLUME_MARKET_REALITY states the secular volume trend and how it is treated per account rather than as a market average, and SEGMENT_PRINT_PROFILES names, for each targeted segment, the document type that generates the pages, its seasonality, its uptime sensitivity and its buying route

competency_questions.question: How do we build and keep the installed-base intelligence that tells us which account to call and when?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TERRITORY_DEVICE_CENSUS defines what is recorded per account, from which legitimate sources, with a date and confidence label, and EXPIRATION_TIMING_INTELLIGENCE converts a documented end date and notice window into a campaign start date

competency_questions.question: What does our dealer or agent program actually determine about what we can sell, what it costs us, and where our money comes from?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEALER_PROGRAM_MODEL distinguishes the authorized-dealer, direct-branch and agent structures and the mechanism of acquisition cost and program funds, and PRICING_AND_MARGIN_MECHANICS enumerates every place a placement can earn margin plus the guardrail that no margin source may depend on the customer misunderstanding the structure

competency_questions.question: What exactly must a customer be told, in plain language and in writing, before they sign a lease and a service agreement?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCLOSURE_FIRST_STANCE lists the minimum disclosure set and requires it as a delivered one-page term summary rather than a claim that it is in the paperwork, and END_OF_TERM_MECHANICS supplies the auto-renewal, notice-window and return content that summary must carry

competency_questions.question: Which lease structure fits this placement, and how is the monthly payment actually produced?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEASE_INSTRUMENT_ANATOMY explains fair-market-value versus nominal-purchase-option versus fixed-purchase-option structures, the lease rate factor as a mechanism, and everything that can be inside the amount financed, and OFFER_ARCHITECTURE_SELECTION states the criteria that pick a structure and offer shape for this account

competency_questions.question: How is the credit path run, what does a personal guarantee actually commit, and what changes when the lessee is a school district or a city?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LESSOR_AND_CREDIT_PATH describes funder selection, the submission package, advance written disclosure of any guarantee or condition, decline and counter-offer handling, and the non-appropriation and authorization path for public lessees with a verify-in-your-jurisdiction flag

competency_questions.question: How do we quote the per-page service side so that nothing on the first invoices is a surprise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_AGREEMENT_COMMERCIAL_TERMS fixes the structure, the black and colour rate mechanism, the minimum-volume commitment and overage treatment, inclusions and exclusions and escalation, and TOTAL_COST_FRAME shows that cost at the customer's own documented volume

competency_questions.question: How do we build an honest cost comparison against the incumbent without inventing numbers or attacking a competitor?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOTAL_COST_FRAME defines the cost stack, the identical comparison period, the use of the customer's measured volume and the labelling of every assumption, and COMPETITIVE_CONDUCT_ETHICS bounds what may be claimed about the incumbent to what a document supports

competency_questions.question: A prospect is partway through a non-cancellable lease and wants to switch now — what do we do, and what must they be told?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROLLOVER_AND_BUYOUT_DISCLOSURE requires a written payoff quote from the current lessor, a visible rollover line showing the amount and where it lands, its effect on the total of payments and term, and an explicit wait-versus-roll comparison, supported by END_OF_TERM_MECHANICS and EXPIRATION_TIMING_INTELLIGENCE

competency_questions.question: How do we guarantee we never place more device, or a bigger minimum, than the account's real volume justifies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VOLUME_EVIDENCE_GATE forbids configuring or rate-quoting from a guess where evidence is obtainable, defines acceptable evidence and the labelled-assumption-plus-true-up fallback, and forbids undersizing as well as oversizing; OFFER_ARCHITECTURE_SELECTION and SEGMENT_PRINT_PROFILES supply the fit criteria

competency_questions.question: Who actually decides in this account, and what changes when the buyer is a school district, a city or a county?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCOVERY_CONVERSATION captures the decision unit and the customer's own understanding of their agreement, and DECISION_UNIT_AND_PROCUREMENT_PATH maps each role's objection plus the public routes (quote threshold, sealed bid or request for proposal, cooperative contract, board approval, fiscal-year boundary) with the instruction to verify current rules with the entity's purchasing office

competency_questions.question: What must be handled at sale time when the devices will touch patient, student, client or payment information?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATED_SEGMENT_SALES_REQUIREMENTS establishes that the device holds stored images and credentials, names the obligation classes that may apply, requires the return and sanitization expectation to be settled in the documents with who bears the cost, and forbids presenting a device feature as legal compliance

competency_questions.question: What must be true before a signed order is allowed to leave sales and reach the deployment team?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROPOSAL_AND_TERM_SHEET fixes the mandatory contents of the packet and the traceability of every number, and SIGNED_ORDER_HANDOFF states the definition of done: consistent documents, verified authority, acknowledged term summary, attached volume basis, documented credit conditions, payoff and notice obligations with dates, and captured site facts

competency_questions.question: How do we protect a small, unadvised buyer from the pressure our own compensation plan creates?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VULNERABLE_BUYER_CARE names who counts as an unadvised buyer and the added-care behaviours (slower pace, invited independent review, comprehension check, authority confirmation, willingness to decline), and PRICING_AND_MARGIN_MECHANICS names the compensation pressures toward long terms, high minimums and buried rollovers that the care rule counteracts

glossary.definition: The multiplier a leasing company applies to the amount financed to produce the periodic payment. It is not a published price: it is derived from term length, the funder's cost of funds, the assumed residual value of the equipment, the lessee's credit tier and whatever spread the originating dealer adds. Because it is derived per deal and per funder, it must be taken from a current written quote and never quoted from memory or from a market rumour.

A lease in which the lessor retains the residual risk of the equipment, which lowers the periodic payment relative to a financed purchase, and at the end of term the lessee chooses among returning the equipment, renewing, or purchasing it at its then fair market value — an amount that is not fixed at signing and must therefore be disclosed as an unknown driven by device age, condition and market, not as a figure.

A lease, commonly called a one-dollar-out or dollar-buyout lease, in which the lessee may purchase the equipment at the end of term for a nominal or token amount. It is functionally a financed purchase, carries a higher periodic payment than an equivalent fair-market-value structure, and removes the end-of-term return exposure.

An automatic-renewal provision that extends a lease or service agreement for a further defined period — often a further year, sometimes month to month — unless the lessee gives written notice inside a defined window before the scheduled end date. It is the single most common source of anger in this vertical, because it is enforceable, easy to miss and frequently never explained at signing.

The period, defined in the agreement, during which a lessee's written non-renewal or return notice is valid. It can both open and close months before the final payment, may require a specific delivery method and recipient, and is the operative date for campaign timing: a proposal that arrives after the window has closed is a proposal for a rollover, not a replacement.

The provision making the lessee's payment obligation to the lessor unconditional and independent of any dispute with the dealer over equipment, service or promises. Its practical meaning — that switching service providers or being unhappy with the machine does not stop the lease payments — is a mandatory disclosure item, not a technicality.

The per-impression charge, often called a click charge, under a service agreement, normally quoted at separate rates for black and colour pages and covering a defined set of parts, labour and consumables. What the rate includes and excludes, and how a colour page is counted, matter as much as the rate itself; the rate is set per agreement and per funder-independent service structure, so it is described here as a mechanism to be verified against a written quote.

A committed number of pages billed each period whether or not they are printed, with pages above that number billed at an overage rate. The commitment is what converts a page-based agreement into a predictable annuity for the dealer and the main way a customer can be quietly overcharged; whether unused pages roll over, and how the commitment was derived from evidenced volume, are disclosure items.

The practice of paying off a customer's remaining obligation on a prior agreement by adding the payoff amount to the amount financed on a new lease and spreading it over a new, usually longer term. It makes a new monthly payment look competitive while the customer pays for equipment they no longer have. Handled honestly it is a legitimate tool; handled silently it is the vertical's signature abuse.

A provision used when the lessee is a governmental body, allowing the obligation to terminate if the governing board or council does not appropriate funds for a subsequent fiscal period. Public lessees typically require it together with evidence of an authorizing action; the specific requirements vary by jurisdiction and entity type and must be verified currently with the entity's purchasing office and counsel.

nodes.definition: Hold an honest working picture of the market this business sells into. Office print volume per worker has been in long, uneven decline — driven by document management and case management systems, electronic signature, portal delivery replacing mailed paper, electronic filing in courts and agencies, and hybrid schedules that empty an office two days a week — while specific, identifiable pockets keep printing because paper is still the carrier of record for a workflow, not merely a habit. The unit of expert work is refusing two fantasies at once: the vendor fantasy that volumes are flat and a five-year term is therefore safe, and the customer fantasy that they will be paperless next year, which almost never lands on schedule. Everything downstream inherits this judgement: how long a term may honestly be offered, how large a minimum-volume commitment may be, how much device is justified, and which segments deserve a representative's calendar at all. Volume trajectory is treated as a per-account measured quantity with a direction, never as a market average applied to a particular clinic or district.

included: the direction and drivers of page volume in office environments
the effect of volume trajectory on honest term length and minimum commitments
per-account trajectory as a measured quantity rather than a market average
excluded: measuring a specific account's pages, which is the fleet-assessment knowledge base
the realized economics of pages already under contract, which is the economics knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: aggregated meter histories from the installed base show a segment's pages moving against the assumed trajectory, or a customer workflow change lands at scale in a targeted segment

pros.claim: Anchoring term length and minimum commitments to a volume direction rather than to last year's page count prevents the classic overcommitment that ends in a dispute
pros.example: declining to write a long term with a high monthly minimum for a firm that is midway through a document-management rollout it expects to finish inside two years

pros.claim: Saying out loud that pages are declining earns credibility with buyers who have heard every competitor insist otherwise, and it makes the rest of the conversation easier
pros.example: opening with the observation that the customer's own meters show fewer pages each year and asking what changed, instead of pitching a bigger machine

cons.claim: A decline narrative applied bluntly leads a team to abandon segments whose volume is actually stable or growing
cons.example: writing off title and escrow offices for being 'paperless' when every closing still produces a signed paper packet per file

cons.claim: Trajectory evidence at the account level is scarce early in a relationship, so the judgement often has to be made on a single meter snapshot and the customer's own plans
cons.example: having one month of meter data and a stated intention to adopt e-signature, with no way to know which way the next year goes

failure_modes: quoting a term longer than the customer's own confidence in their volume, then defending it later with the contract
applying a market-wide decline rate to a specific account instead of asking what generates that account's pages
converting the decline into a fear lever — implying prices or rates will rise so the customer should sign today
acceptance_tests: every proposed term length and minimum commitment can be justified out loud by reference to that account's own volume direction and stated plans, not by a market generalisation
revisit_triggers: meter histories across several accounts in a segment move materially against the assumed direction
a workflow change lands in a segment at scale, such as an electronic-filing mandate or a district-wide device policy

nodes.definition: Maintain a working profile of each segment that still carries office page volume, built around the document that generates the pages, because the generator determines the device class, the durability of the volume and the way the segment buys. Legal practices print discovery productions, exhibit sets, closing binders and client files; volume follows case load and spikes around trial and filing calendars, and confidentiality expectations are high. Medical practices and clinics print chart summaries, referral packets, after-visit instructions and payer forms; volume follows visit counts and carries patient-information handling duties. Schools and districts print worksheets, assessment packets, programme and athletics material; volume is shaped by the academic calendar with a summer trough and a start-of-year spike, and buying runs on budget cycles and bid rules. Logistics and distribution print bills of lading, packing lists, labels and proof of delivery; volume follows shipments and tolerates almost no downtime because a truck waits when a printer stops. Municipal offices, courts and utilities print agendas and board packets, permits, notices and records responses; volume follows the meeting calendar and buying is public and rule-bound. Adjacent pockets — title and escrow, insurance agencies, accounting in season, houses of worship with weekly bulletins — behave similarly. Each profile records the page generator, the seasonality, the uptime sensitivity, the finishing needs such as stapling, booklet making or hole punching, and the buying route.

included: the document type that generates pages in each segment
seasonality, uptime sensitivity and finishing implications
the buying route that segment uses and what qualifies an account as worth pursuing
excluded: a specific account's measured volume and device-level right-sizing
service delivery staffing and response logistics for that segment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: won/lost records and installed-base meters in a segment contradict its stated page generator, seasonality or buying route

pros.claim: Knowing the page generator turns a guess about a prospect into a testable question, so qualification takes one conversation instead of three visits
pros.example: asking a distribution manager how many shipments leave per shift, because bills of lading and packing lists scale directly with that number

pros.claim: Profiling uptime sensitivity by segment lets the offer be shaped where it matters rather than discounted everywhere
pros.example: leading with response commitments and a backup device for a three-shift dock, and leading with cost per page for a back-office accounting group

cons.claim: Segment averages mislead badly on any single account, and a representative who trusts the profile over the meter will misconfigure the deal
cons.example: a law firm that moved to electronic filing and now prints less than the twelve-person marketing agency in the same building

cons.claim: Profiles decay as workflows change, and maintaining them competes with selling time
cons.example: a district adopting one-to-one devices and cutting worksheet printing across every school in a single budget year

failure_modes: treating a segment label as a volume estimate and configuring from it
chasing a segment because a competitor is winning there rather than because its page generator is durable
ignoring seasonality and setting a flat minimum commitment for an account whose volume is concentrated in a few months
acceptance_tests: each targeted segment profile names its page generator, its seasonality, its uptime sensitivity and its buying route, and a representative can state them without notes
no account is configured from its segment profile alone; the profile only sets the questions asked
revisit_triggers: a segment adopts a workflow that removes or adds a document class, such as electronic filing, portal statements or one-to-one student devices
won and lost outcomes in a segment stop matching the profile's assumptions about who buys and why

nodes.definition: Assemble and continuously maintain an account-by-account picture of the territory's installed base: which organizations run which device classes, roughly how many and how old, who the incumbent dealer is, which leasing company holds the paper, when the current agreement is scheduled to end, what the notice window is, and what the customer believes about all of it. The data is gathered legitimately and incrementally — from the customer when they choose to share, from what is visible on a walkthrough such as the device's own configuration page, meter display and the lessor's asset label, from the customer's own invoices when they show them, from public bid records, award notices, board minutes and cooperative-contract listings for public entities, and from the dealer's own service history and prior quotes. Every fact is stored with its source, the date it was captured and a confidence label, because expiry dates are usually given from memory and are frequently wrong; contract end date and notice deadline are stored as two distinct fields because they are two distinct dates. The census is the fuel of the sales engine: without it a representative meets an account three weeks after its automatic renewal has already locked, and the census belongs to the company rather than to a representative's notebook.

included: per-account device, incumbent, lessor, end-date and notice-window records
legitimate collection sources and the source, date and confidence label on every fact
won and lost outcomes fed back so the account re-enters the calendar at the right time
excluded: detailed device-level assessment and meter capture, which belongs to the fleet-assessment knowledge base
management of accounts already under the dealer's own agreements, which belongs to the economics and renewal knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a document produced by the customer, an observed new installation, or a recorded win/loss contradicts a stored account record

pros.claim: A dated, sourced expiry record converts a cold account into a scheduled campaign with months of runway instead of a rushed rescue
pros.example: knowing in the autumn that a county department's agreement ends the following summer with a notice deadline in the spring, and planning backwards from the notice date

pros.claim: Holding the intelligence as a company asset survives representative turnover, which in this trade is the main way territory knowledge is lost
pros.example: a new representative inheriting sourced records instead of restarting discovery on two hundred accounts

cons.claim: The census decays quickly and a stale record is worse than no record because it schedules the call confidently at the wrong time
cons.example: an end date captured two years earlier that missed a mid-term upgrade which reset the whole agreement

cons.claim: Maintaining it consumes selling hours that produce no immediate revenue, so it is the first discipline abandoned under quota pressure
cons.example: a quarter where nobody updates dates and the following year's calendar has gaps nobody notices until the renewals are gone

failure_modes: recording a date the customer guessed and then treating it as fact in campaign planning
accepting an incumbent's confidential documents from a departing employee or a contact who should not have them
storing a single end date and losing the notice deadline, which is the date that actually governs
letting the census live in personal notebooks and phones so it leaves with the representative
acceptance_tests: every date and rate in the census carries a source, a capture date and a confidence label
contract end date and notice deadline are stored as separate fields, and no campaign is scheduled from an unsourced date
revisit_triggers: an incumbent installs new equipment at a tracked account, which usually resets the whole agreement
the customer produces an actual document whose dates or terms differ from the recorded ones
a loss is recorded and the winning agreement's term becomes the next campaign date

nodes.definition: Understand precisely which model you operate under, because it fixes what you are allowed to sell, what your equipment actually costs you, and which obligations you carry after the sale. The common structures are: an authorized independent dealer holding one or more manufacturer lines under a dealer agreement, with expectations around territory, product-line breadth, technician certification, demonstration capability and reporting, and with back-end mechanisms such as volume tiers, marketing or co-operative funds and deal-specific special pricing approvals; a manufacturer's own direct branch, where pricing authority and program funds work differently; a master-dealer or agency arrangement in which another party holds the service obligation and the paper and you are compensated on placement; and multi-line dealers who blend these. What matters commercially is the mechanism rather than any figure: acquisition cost is a function of program tier plus any approved deal-specific pricing rather than a published list; program funds are earned against conditions and can be reduced or clawed back; supplies and parts terms flow from the same agreement; and certification determines which environments you can legitimately serve. The model also determines your exposure if a line is lost or a manufacturer changes program terms, which is why the installed base's service obligation, not just the current margin, is part of the assessment.

included: authorized dealer, direct branch, master-dealer and agent structures and what each obliges
the mechanism of acquisition cost, program tiers, special pricing and program funds
line breadth and certification as a constraint on what can honestly be offered
excluded: any specific discount, tier threshold or fund amount stated as fact
service delivery capacity planning and parts logistics, which belong to the deployment and economics knowledge bases

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a manufacturer or master dealer issues changed program terms, tier thresholds, fund conditions or certification requirements

pros.claim: Knowing where cost actually comes from prevents quoting a price the program cannot support and then discovering it at funding
pros.example: confirming whether a competitive placement qualifies for special pricing before promising a payment to a district

pros.claim: Multi-line breadth lets an operator fit segments honestly instead of forcing one manufacturer's device into every environment
pros.example: having a robust production-capable line for a print-heavy municipal print room and a simpler line for small clinics

cons.claim: Program tiers and fund conditions create a standing pull toward whichever line pays best rather than whichever line fits
cons.example: an approaching tier threshold tempting a team to place a device that is wrong for the account's finishing needs

cons.claim: Breadth splits volume across lines, weakening tier position and multiplying certification, demonstration and parts obligations
cons.example: carrying three lines and holding tier standing in none of them, so every deal needs a special pricing request

failure_modes: quoting from an assumed cost rather than a current approved cost and losing the margin at funding
promising service or supplies terms that the dealer agreement does not actually provide
letting a program incentive select the device before the account's evidence has selected it
carrying an installed base on a line whose future you have not questioned
acceptance_tests: every quoted configuration traces to a current cost position — standard program cost or a written special-pricing approval — before the number reaches a customer
the obligations the dealer carries after placement (service, supplies, certification) are stated in the offer rather than assumed
revisit_triggers: a manufacturer changes program terms, tier structure, fund conditions or territory expectations
a line is added, lost or repositioned, which changes both what can be offered and what the installed base needs

nodes.definition: Operate a standing, non-negotiable rule that every commercially material term of the lease and the service agreement is stated in plain language, in writing, before signature, and is also walked through out loud — because the reputational damage this vertical carries comes almost entirely from terms that were technically in the document and never explained. The minimum disclosure set is fixed and does not vary by deal size: how many payments there are, how often they fall and what each payment does and does not include; whether service, consumables, black pages and colour pages sit inside the payment or are billed separately; the minimum volume commitment and exactly how overage is charged; whether and by what mechanism payments or page rates escalate; who the leasing company is, and that the lease is a separate obligation from service which typically continues to be payable even if the customer is unhappy with the equipment or the servicing dealer; what happens at the end of term, specifically whether it renews automatically absent written notice, when the notice window opens and closes and how notice must be delivered; what must be returned, in what condition, packed by whom and at whose freight cost; whether a personal guarantee is being requested; and any pass-throughs such as property tax, insurance requirements or administrative fees. Disclosure is a delivered artifact — a one-page plain-language term summary that the customer keeps, alongside the contract — and never the claim that it is all in the paperwork.

included: the fixed minimum disclosure set for lease and service terms
the plain-language term summary as a delivered, acknowledged artifact
the verbal walkthrough and comprehension check before signature
excluded: legal advice on enforceability or on the customer's accounting treatment
the drafting of the lessor's contract language itself, which the dealer does not control

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a customer dispute, a regulator or association guidance note, or a lessor contract change alters what must appear in the minimum disclosure set

pros.claim: Disclosed terms convert the end of a lease from the moment a customer discovers what they signed into the moment the next agreement is discussed
pros.example: a customer who was told at signing when their notice window opens calling the dealer to plan the refresh instead of calling a lawyer about an automatic renewal

pros.claim: A fixed disclosure set removes discretion from the representative, which protects both the customer and the company from a single person's shortcut
pros.example: a new representative who cannot omit the guarantee or the return freight because the summary template will not produce without them

cons.claim: Full disclosure lengthens the close and loses deals to competitors who say less, particularly on small placements where the buyer wants it over quickly
cons.example: a two-partner office signing the same week with a competitor whose paperwork took ten minutes and whose renewal clause was never mentioned

cons.claim: Reading every term aloud can frighten an inexperienced buyer out of a placement that would genuinely serve them
cons.example: a small nonprofit hearing the words non-cancellable and personal guarantee together and abandoning a sensible replacement of a failing device

failure_modes: treating the signature on the contract as evidence that the terms were understood
disclosing everything in writing but burying it in a proposal appendix nobody reads aloud
letting the disclosure standard slip on small deals where the representative judges it unnecessary
presenting the summary after the customer has already signed the finance documents
acceptance_tests: every signed order is accompanied by a term summary that covers each item in the minimum disclosure set, acknowledged by the customer, with a copy retained by them
the customer can restate, in their own words, what happens at the end of the term and what they must do to avoid an automatic renewal
no proposal leaves the office without the escalation mechanism, the minimum commitment and the overage mechanism written in plain language
revisit_triggers: a complaint or dispute traces to a term the customer says was never explained
a lessor or manufacturer changes contract language, notice mechanics or fee schedules
an audit of recent orders finds term summaries missing, incomplete or signed after the finance documents

nodes.definition: Recognize the buyers in this market who have no procurement function, no counsel reading the lease and no prior experience of a multi-year non-cancellable instrument — a two-partner clinic, a parish or synagogue office, a volunteer-run nonprofit, a small rural district or fire authority, a sole proprietor, an owner near retirement, a newly promoted office manager signing their first equipment contract — and apply added care rather than added pressure. In practice: slow the pace deliberately; put the plain-language term summary in their hands and invite them to have their attorney, accountant, board treasurer or business officer read it before signing; never present a signature as time-limited unless a genuine, documented program or quote expiry exists and can be shown; do not stack the equipment order and the finance documents into one hurried signing session; check comprehension by asking them to state the end-of-term obligation and the payment total back in their own words; confirm that the person signing actually holds authority, which for a nonprofit, congregation or public body means an authorizing action rather than whoever is at the desk; and be willing to shrink the configuration, shorten the term or decline the deal outright when the payment is out of proportion to evidenced volume or the term outruns the buyer's own planning horizon. The rule is that a buyer's inexperience is never a commercial opportunity.

included: identifying buyers without advisory or procurement capacity
pacing, invited independent review, comprehension checks and authority verification
the duty to shrink, restructure or decline rather than place a disproportionate obligation
excluded: giving the buyer financial, tax or legal advice in place of their own advisor
any assessment of the buyer's personal circumstances beyond what the placement requires

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: complaints, rescission requests or reviews concentrate among small unadvised buyers, or the compensation plan changes the pressure on closing pace

pros.claim: Care converts the highest-complaint-risk segment of the book into its most loyal part, because these buyers stay for a decade when they are treated well
pros.example: a congregation that replaces its device with the same dealer three cycles running because nothing was ever a surprise

pros.claim: Verifying authority and inviting review pre-empts the disputes that are most expensive to unwind after funding
pros.example: waiting for a board vote rather than accepting an office administrator's signature on a five-year obligation

cons.claim: Slowing down and inviting outside review loses deals that a faster competitor closes in the same week
cons.example: a clinic manager signing with the competitor who arrived the next morning while the customer's accountant was still reading the summary

cons.claim: Judgements about who is vulnerable are subjective and can slide into condescension or into an excuse for not asking for the order
cons.example: treating an experienced small-business owner as if they could not read a term summary and stalling a straightforward decision

failure_modes: manufacturing urgency with an expiry that cannot be evidenced
obtaining a signature from someone without authority because they were willing to sign
presenting a personal guarantee as a formality to a buyer who has never given one
placing a payment that the account's evidenced volume cannot support because the buyer did not push back
acceptance_tests: for any buyer without procurement or advisory capacity, the file shows the term summary delivered before the signing session and an explicit invitation to have an advisor review it
the file records who signed, the basis of their authority, and — for a board, council or congregation — the authorizing action
any urgency communicated to the customer is backed by a documented program or quote expiry date on file
revisit_triggers: a complaint, cancellation attempt or negative review comes from a small or unadvised buyer
compensation or quota structure changes in a way that increases pressure to close quickly

nodes.definition: Compete against an incumbent on verifiable facts alone, in a trade where the temptation to do otherwise is constant because the customer usually cannot check. What is legitimate and effective: comparing the customer's own documented costs against a written proposal on an identical basis; working from what the customer themselves reports about response times and downtime; quoting device capability from the manufacturer's own published specifications; and reading the customer's existing agreement with them, clause by clause, so they understand their real position. What is not legitimate: asserting defects in a competitor's equipment or company that you cannot evidence; misrepresenting what the customer's current contract says in order to make switching look urgent or costless; claiming an incumbent is failing, losing its line or leaving the market without a public, citable basis; manufacturing price-increase urgency; using data-security or compliance fear as a closing lever; using confidential competitor documents obtained from a departing employee or a contact who should not have them; and disparaging an individual representative. The node also covers the mirror image — how to answer misinformation aimed at you without escalating: return to the document, offer to read the relevant clause together, put the correction in writing, and where the claim concerns authorization or capability, let the manufacturer or a reference confirm it.

included: what may and may not be claimed about an incumbent, its equipment and its contracts
the prohibition on fear-based and urgency-based closing levers
responding to misinformation about your own company with documents rather than escalation
excluded: the cost comparison method itself, which is the total-cost node
any legal opinion on a competitor's contract or conduct

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a documented incident in which a competitive claim by either side proved false, or new association or advertising guidance on comparative claims

pros.claim: A representative who never has to remember which story they told can sell the same way in front of any audience, including the customer's counsel
pros.example: reading the prospect's own renewal clause aloud with them rather than characterising what a competitor supposedly did

pros.claim: Refusing fear levers protects the account when the fear turns out to be wrong, which in a small market gets back to everyone
pros.example: declining to tell a clinic that its current device puts it in breach of privacy rules, and instead asking what their compliance owner requires

cons.claim: Restraint is asymmetric: the competitor who exaggerates often wins the meeting, and the honest version is less exciting
cons.example: losing to a rival who promised savings and a costless exit from a lease that in fact had a substantial payoff

cons.claim: Correcting misinformation without attacking is slow, requires documents in hand, and sometimes reads as defensiveness
cons.example: needing a manufacturer authorization letter and two references to answer a rumour that took a competitor one sentence to start

failure_modes: characterising a competitor's contract from memory and being wrong in the customer's favour, which becomes a promise
using a compliance or security concern as a closing device rather than as a question for the customer's compliance owner
accepting a competitor's confidential pricing from a contact and using it
answering a rumour by starting one
acceptance_tests: every competitive claim in a proposal or meeting can be traced to a document: the customer's own paperwork, published manufacturer specifications, or a written quote
no urgency, price-increase or compliance-risk statement is made to a customer without a document that supports it on file
revisit_triggers: a competitor's claim about the dealer circulates in the territory and must be answered with documents
a win or loss review shows a deal turned on an unevidenced claim by either side

nodes.definition: Know the instrument itself cold, because everything the customer experiences for the next several years is produced by it. Office equipment is normally placed on a commercial equipment lease written by a third-party leasing company or a manufacturer's captive finance arm and assigned away from the dealer when the deal funds, which means the dealer sells the offer while the funder owns the paper. The structures differ mainly in who carries residual risk: a fair-market-value lease leaves the residual with the lessor, produces a lower periodic payment and ends in a return, renewal or purchase-at-market decision; a nominal purchase option lease is functionally a financed purchase with a higher payment and no residual exposure; a fixed-purchase-option structure sits between them with the end price named at signing. The payment itself is produced by applying a lease rate factor to the amount financed, and both halves of that product must be understood: the factor is derived from term length, the funder's cost of funds, assumed residual, credit tier and any spread the originating dealer adds, and the amount financed can contain far more than the machine — delivery and installation, soft costs, a buyout absorbed from a prior agreement, and sometimes bundled service. The standing clauses that must be read and explained are the unconditional payment obligation, assignment, insurance and property-tax responsibilities, late and administrative fee schedules, relocation and assignment restrictions, and how the lease document interacts with the separate service agreement. The operating rule: never quote a payment without knowing which structure it is and exactly what is inside the amount financed.

included: lease structures and their end-of-term consequences
the lease rate factor and the amount financed as mechanisms
the standing clauses that must be read and disclosed at sale time
excluded: any specific factor, rate or payment figure asserted as market fact
the customer's accounting or tax treatment of the lease, which belongs to their advisors

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a funder issues revised lease documents, fee schedules or end-of-term procedures, or a dispute shows a clause operating differently than explained

pros.claim: Understanding how a payment is produced lets a representative explain a competitor's lower payment without implying dishonesty, and defend a higher one without discounting
pros.example: showing that a rival's lower payment comes from a longer term and a fair-market-value structure rather than from cheaper equipment

pros.claim: Reading the standing clauses at sale time makes the end of the term predictable for both sides, which is where the next placement comes from
pros.example: explaining at signing that the payment obligation continues even if the customer later changes service providers, so nobody is surprised in year four

cons.claim: The same literacy is exactly what makes cost easy to hide inside term length and the amount financed, so the knowledge is dangerous without the disclosure rule bolted to it
cons.example: lengthening a term to absorb a buyout so the payment looks flat while the total of payments rises sharply

cons.claim: The dealer controls neither the funder's boilerplate nor its end-of-term administration, so explaining a document you cannot change carries risk of misstatement
cons.example: describing a return process the leasing company later administers differently than the representative expected

failure_modes: quoting a payment without knowing the structure behind it, then discovering the end-of-term consequence at term end
letting soft costs and buyouts accumulate inside the amount financed without a line-by-line statement
explaining the customer's obligations from memory instead of from the document in front of you
assuming the service agreement and the lease end on the same date
acceptance_tests: every quoted payment is accompanied by the structure name, the number and frequency of payments, and an itemised statement of what is inside the amount financed
a representative can explain, without notes, the difference between a fair-market-value and a nominal purchase option ending, and the meaning of the unconditional payment clause
revisit_triggers: a funder changes its documents, fee schedule, or end-of-term administration
a customer dispute reveals that a clause was explained differently from how the funder applies it

nodes.definition: Run the credit path as its own unit of work, on the understanding that the dealer does not make the credit decision and must never imply otherwise. The work has four parts. First, choosing where to submit: a captive finance arm, an independent leasing company or a bank program, selected on which structures they write, their appetite for the customer's industry and size, how they administer end of term, and how they treat public lessees. Second, assembling the submission: application, exact legal entity name and structure, time in business, and for larger amounts sometimes financial statements or bank information — and telling the customer in advance what will be requested and what will be pulled. Third, disclosing conditions before they appear: whether a personal guarantee will be asked, which converts a business obligation into a personal one and is the most under-disclosed item in small-business placements; whether advance payments, a deposit or a shorter term will be required; and what happens if the funder declines, so a counter-offer is presented as a choice rather than as a fait accompli at the signing table. Fourth, the public path, which is a different animal: governmental lessees normally require a non-appropriation or fiscal-funding clause, an authorizing action by the board or council, and sometimes an opinion or specific document set, and the rules differ by jurisdiction and entity type and change — name the obligation class, verify current requirements with the entity's purchasing office and your funder, and never advise a public body about its own legal authority.

included: funder selection criteria and the submission package
advance written disclosure of guarantees, advance payments and other conditions
decline and counter-offer handling, and the public-lessee documentation path
excluded: credit adjudication itself, which is the funder's decision
advising a customer or a public body on its own authority, solvency or accounting treatment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a funder publishes changed credit, guarantee or public-entity documentation requirements, or declines cluster in a targeted segment

pros.claim: Disclosing a guarantee before submission rather than at signature removes the most common late-stage collapse in small-business placements
pros.example: telling a two-owner practice at proposal time that a personal guarantee is likely, so the partners decide together rather than at the table

pros.claim: Choosing the funder deliberately — including on how it administers end of term — prevents inheriting somebody else's return process as your reputation
pros.example: preferring a funder whose return instructions and notice handling the dealer can explain accurately to a school district

cons.claim: The dealer carries the relationship consequences of decisions it does not make, including declines, conditions and administration it cannot change
cons.example: explaining to a long-standing customer that the funder now wants advance payments and a guarantee after a soft year

cons.claim: Public-entity documentation is slow and jurisdiction-specific, and getting it wrong can void the transaction after delivery
cons.example: a district signature obtained before the board's authorizing action, leaving the placement unsupported

failure_modes: submitting an application before telling the customer what will be pulled and what may be required
presenting a counter-offer with a guarantee attached at the signing table as if it were the original deal
treating a public lessee like a commercial one and omitting the non-appropriation and authorization path
implying the dealer approves credit, or promising approval
acceptance_tests: any personal guarantee, advance payment or other funding condition is disclosed to the customer in writing before the application is submitted
public-entity files contain the non-appropriation provision and evidence of the authorizing action before delivery is scheduled
the file names the funder, the structure submitted and the date of the current written quote used to build the payment
revisit_triggers: a funder changes credit appetite, documentation requirements or its treatment of public lessees
a decline or conditional approval pattern emerges in a segment the dealer targets

nodes.definition: Master what actually happens when an agreement approaches its end, because that is where this vertical's customer anger concentrates and where the next placement is won or lost. The mechanics that must be known cold and explained plainly: many agreements renew automatically for a further period unless written notice is delivered inside a defined window before the scheduled end date, and that window can open and close months before the last payment, may require a particular delivery method and a particular recipient, and is not satisfied by telling a sales representative; end-of-term options depend on the structure, running from return, to renewal, to purchase at a fair market value that is not fixed at signing, to purchase at a stated option price; return obligations typically include de-installation, correct packing, freight to a designated location and a condition standard, with charges for damage, missing accessories or unreturned units; and continued use past the end date accrues holdover charges. On the selling side this knowledge does two jobs at once: it guarantees your own customer is never surprised by any of it, and it lets you read a prospect's existing agreement accurately to establish their true dates, notice obligations and return exposure before promising them anything about switching.

included: automatic renewal, notice windows and valid notice delivery
end-of-term options by structure, return condition and freight obligations, holdover charges
reading a prospect's existing agreement to establish their real exposure
excluded: administering the dealer's own installed-base renewals and the upgrade-versus-extend-versus-return decision on owned accounts, which belongs to the economics and renewal knowledge base
legal opinion on the enforceability of a renewal or return provision

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a funder changes renewal, notice or return administration, or a returned fleet is charged in a way the disclosed process did not anticipate

pros.claim: Knowing exactly how notice must be given lets a dealer help a prospect protect themselves, which is the most credible act available in this trade
pros.example: showing a prospect the address and deadline their own agreement requires for a non-renewal letter, whether or not they buy

pros.claim: Accurate return exposure turns a vague switching conversation into arithmetic that both sides can check
pros.example: identifying that a departing fleet must be de-installed, packed and freighted at the customer's cost before quoting a replacement

cons.claim: The dealer explains a process another company administers, so a misstatement becomes the dealer's problem even when the funder's practice changed
cons.example: a customer told returns were collected who is later invoiced for freight and packing by the leasing company

cons.claim: Raising renewal and return exposure early can persuade a prospect to do nothing at all for another year
cons.example: a prospect who, on learning their window has closed, stops the conversation instead of planning the next cycle

failure_modes: assuming a notice window opens near the final payment when it opens far earlier
letting a customer believe that telling a representative counts as notice
quoting a fair-market-value buyout as if it were a known number
ignoring accessory, condition and freight charges when comparing keep-versus-return
acceptance_tests: for the dealer's own placements, the notice window opening date, closing date, delivery method and recipient appear on the term summary the customer keeps
for a prospect, dates and obligations quoted back to them are taken from their own document, with the document identified, and never from recollection
revisit_triggers: a funder changes notice, return or holdover practice
a customer or prospect reports being charged at return in a way the process description did not predict

nodes.definition: Quote the service side as an explicit commercial structure rather than as a bundled mystery, because the page agreement is where the annuity lives and where the customer's sense of fairness is decided every month. The shapes in common use are a cost-per-page agreement with separate black and colour rates, usually with a minimum volume commitment and per-page overage above it; a base charge plus clicks; a flat all-inclusive monthly charge per device; and supplies-only or parts-and-labour variants. What must be settled in writing at quote time: which consumables are included, since toner almost always is while staples, waste containers, imaging units and paper are the recurring arguments; what is excluded, typically paper, operator abuse, network and workstation troubleshooting, relocations and non-standard media; how a colour page is counted and whether any tiered or low-coverage treatment applies; whether unused minimum pages roll forward; the escalation mechanism and whether it is capped; the term of the service agreement and how it relates to the lease term, which frequently differs and must be stated; and the response commitment expressed as the dealer will actually staff it. The selling-side rule is that the rate mechanism and the volume assumption behind the minimum are both written down and explained. How that coverage is then delivered belongs to the deployment knowledge base, and what it actually costs the dealer per page belongs to the economics knowledge base.

included: the commercial shape of the page agreement as quoted and disclosed
inclusions, exclusions, colour counting, minimums, overage, roll-forward and escalation
the relationship between service term and lease term
excluded: service activation, coverage setup, consumable replenishment and response staffing as delivered operations
realized service cost per page, parts consumption and margin control on the installed base
meter-read collection and billing integrity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: billed volumes and mix on comparable accounts diverge from the assumptions used to set minimums, or inclusion policy for parts and consumables changes

pros.claim: An explicit structure makes the first invoices match the sales conversation, which is the single strongest predictor of whether the account renews
pros.example: a customer whose first colour-heavy month lands exactly where the quoted mechanism said it would

pros.claim: Writing exclusions down protects both sides from the arguments this trade is famous for
pros.example: stating at quote time that relocations and network troubleshooting are billable, so a later move is a conversation and not a grievance

cons.claim: A fully explicit structure is harder to sell than one all-in number, and competitors will present a simpler-looking quote
cons.example: a buyer comparing a transparent base-plus-overage quote against a single monthly figure that quietly contains a minimum

cons.claim: Minimum commitments that were fair at signing become unfair as volumes decline, and the customer experiences the mechanism as a trap
cons.example: an office that halved its printing after a workflow change still paying a committed volume for the remaining term

failure_modes: quoting a page rate before the black and colour mix is known
leaving imaging units, staples or waste containers ambiguous and arguing about them later
letting the service term and the lease term differ without telling the customer
setting the minimum at the volume the dealer wants rather than at the volume the evidence supports
acceptance_tests: every page-based quote states the black and colour rate basis, the minimum commitment and its volume basis, the overage mechanism, inclusions, exclusions, escalation and both terms
the minimum commitment can be traced to documented volume evidence or to a labelled assumption with a true-up mechanism
revisit_triggers: the account's actual page mix or volume diverges materially from the basis the minimum was set on
a manufacturer or dealer changes what consumables and parts are treated as included

nodes.definition: Build the comparison the customer actually needs — a like-for-like total cost over a stated period, assembled from a defined stack rather than reduced to one attractive monthly number. The stack has seven layers: the financed payment, with how many payments there are at what frequency plus any advance payments; the page-based service cost computed at the customer's own documented volume and mix, including the minimum commitment and realistic overage; consumables and items not included; delivery, installation, network integration and training where these are charged; end-of-term cost, which is either return freight, de-installation and condition exposure or the buyout if the customer intends to keep the equipment; taxes and documented pass-throughs such as property tax and administrative fees; and any rollover of a prior obligation carried into the new agreement. The method's integrity rules are what make it worth anything: use measured volume rather than a flattering assumption; hold the comparison period identical across every option including the incumbent's; show the black and colour split explicitly because colour usually dominates the service line; state every assumption as an assumption on the page; and where a number genuinely cannot be known — future overage, a fair-market-value buyout, a future escalation — present the mechanism and what drives it rather than inventing a figure to make the total look finished.

included: the seven-layer cost stack and the identical-period comparison discipline
assumption labelling and the mechanism-not-figure rule for unknowables
normalising an incumbent or competitor quote onto the same basis
excluded: advising the customer on financing, tax or accounting treatment of any option
the dealer's own internal cost and margin analysis, which is a separate unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-sale invoice history on comparable accounts diverges from the totals the comparison method predicted

pros.claim: A stack comparison survives scrutiny by a controller or a purchasing officer, which is exactly where single-number quotes fall apart
pros.example: a finance director able to reconcile the proposal's total against the customer's own invoice history line by line

pros.claim: Labelling unknowables as mechanisms keeps the proposal honest without leaving a blank, and it pre-frames the end-of-term conversation
pros.example: presenting a fair-market-value ending as an option whose price depends on device age and condition rather than quoting a number nobody can know

cons.claim: The honest total is usually larger and less exciting than a competitor's monthly figure, and some buyers only look at the monthly figure
cons.example: losing a small office that compared one line of a rival quote against a two-page cost stack

cons.claim: Building it properly takes time and depends on data the customer may not want to release
cons.example: a prospect who will not share invoices, leaving half the incumbent side of the comparison as labelled assumption

failure_modes: comparing a shorter term against a longer one without normalising the period
using an optimistic colour mix that makes the service line look small
omitting end-of-term cost from one side of the comparison
presenting a projected saving as a guarantee rather than as arithmetic conditional on stated volume
acceptance_tests: both sides of any comparison cover the same number of months, the same volume and mix, and the same inclusion set, with differences called out
every figure in the comparison traces to the customer's data, a written quote or an explicitly labelled assumption
no unknowable amount appears as a specific number without the mechanism that produces it
revisit_triggers: the customer releases invoices or meters that change the volume or mix basis
a competing quote arrives on a different basis and must be normalised
escalation, fee or pass-through practice changes at the funder or dealer

nodes.definition: Time the campaign to the account's contract calendar rather than to your own quota calendar, which is the difference between a clean competitive displacement and an expensive rescue. The work: establish from documents rather than memory the contract end date, the date the notice window opens and closes, the number of payments remaining and whether an automatic renewal has already fired; then work backwards to a contact sequence that puts a decision in front of the buying unit early enough for a valid non-renewal notice to be given and for the incumbent's inevitable counter-offer to be considered calmly. Enter too late and the only deal available is an early termination or a rolled buyout, which costs the customer money and costs you the moral high ground; enter far too early and you spend credibility on a conversation the customer cannot act on, while your intelligence goes stale. Public entities carry a second, often more binding calendar: budget adoption, board or council meeting dates, and any quote-threshold or bid requirement that adds months to the path. Losses are recorded with the date the incumbent's new agreement ends so the account re-enters the calendar rather than disappearing.

included: deriving campaign start dates from documented notice windows and end dates
layering the public budget, board and bid calendar over the contract calendar
recording losses with the next opportunity date
excluded: the renewal calendar of the dealer's own installed base, which belongs to the economics and renewal knowledge base
the content of the offer itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: documents produced by prospects, observed mid-term upgrades, or published board and budget calendars change the derived campaign dates

pros.claim: Campaigns keyed to the notice window arrive when the customer can actually act, which raises win rate without any change to price
pros.example: presenting three months before a notice deadline so the customer can give proper notice and still evaluate two proposals

pros.claim: Recording the loss date keeps a territory finite: nothing is permanently gone, it is only scheduled
pros.example: logging a lost district with its new agreement end date and its notice window, and being first in the following cycle

cons.claim: Calendar discipline conflicts with quarterly quota pressure and tempts a team to pull deals forward through rollovers
cons.example: a quarter-end push that converts three well-timed campaigns into three mid-term buyouts

cons.claim: Documented dates are often unobtainable until the prospect trusts you enough to show the paperwork, so early planning runs on soft data
cons.example: a gatekeeper who will not share the agreement, leaving the campaign timed on an educated guess

failure_modes: timing a campaign from a remembered date and arriving after the notice window has closed
ignoring a public entity's budget and board calendar so a good proposal misses the only meeting that mattered
treating the last payment date as the deadline when the notice deadline came months earlier
abandoning a lost account instead of diarising it
acceptance_tests: each active campaign's start date derives from a documented notice window or, where undocumented, is explicitly flagged as an estimate to be confirmed
public-sector campaigns carry the entity's budget adoption and board meeting dates alongside the contract dates
every loss record carries the date the account should be re-approached
revisit_triggers: the prospect produces a document that changes the dates
an incumbent performs a mid-term upgrade that resets the agreement
a public entity changes its meeting or budget calendar

nodes.definition: Run a disciplined discovery that produces facts rather than enthusiasm. What is established: which documents the organization actually produces and who produces them; where the pain sits today — downtime and what it costs operationally, service response, surprise invoices, supplies arriving late, scanning that does not reach the document system, colour cost, or people walking too far; what devices exist, how old they are and what people do when one stops; what changed recently and what is planned, since a practice-management or case-management migration, an office move, a headcount change or a new location can move volume more than any device decision; who touches the decision and who can stop it; what the organization's own records say about volume compared with what people believe; and what the customer thinks their current agreement says, which is the fastest way to discover both their exposure and their misconceptions. Discovery also sets honest expectations in the same meeting: what you will need to see — meter readings, an invoice, a walkthrough — before you can quote anything real, and the fact that you will not size a device or commit a page rate from a guess. Discovery is the point at which a health, compliance or savings claim, if the customer raises one, is answered with a mechanism rather than a promise.

included: the discovery question set and its written record
capturing planned workflow changes, the decision unit and the customer's understanding of their own agreement
setting the expectation that evidence precedes any configuration or rate
excluded: the walkthrough and meter capture themselves, which belong to the fleet-assessment knowledge base
any promise about savings, uptime or compliance made in the meeting

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: meter or invoice evidence, or an announced workflow change, contradicts a load-bearing statement recorded in discovery

pros.claim: A written discovery record makes the eventual proposal answer the customer's stated problems in their own words, which is most of persuasion
pros.example: a proposal that opens with the dock supervisor's own sentence about trucks waiting when the label printer stops

pros.claim: Surfacing a planned system migration early prevents placing a fleet sized for a workflow that is about to disappear
pros.example: learning that a clinic goes live on a new patient-records system next quarter, which will end most of its chart printing

cons.claim: A long discovery burns goodwill with buyers who simply want a price, and some qualified accounts will not sit through it
cons.example: an office manager with three quotes in hand who wants a number by Friday and no interview

cons.claim: Self-reported volume and pain are unreliable and can anchor the whole design before any evidence arrives
cons.example: a customer certain they print heavily whose meters show a fraction of the claim

failure_modes: interviewing only the person who feels the pain and never meeting whoever signs
recording opinions as facts and configuring from them
missing a planned migration because nobody asked what changes next year
answering a customer's savings or compliance question with a promise instead of a mechanism
acceptance_tests: the discovery record captures documents produced, current pains, device inventory, planned changes, the decision unit and the customer's stated understanding of their existing agreement
the record distinguishes what the customer reported from what was observed or documented
revisit_triggers: a planned system migration, move, closure or acquisition is announced during the cycle
evidence arrives that contradicts a materially load-bearing statement from discovery

nodes.definition: Map who decides and by which route, because in this market the person who feels the pain almost never signs. Private accounts typically involve an office or operations manager who owns the daily pain, an information-technology owner who cares about the network, scan destinations, driver deployment and device security posture, a controller or finance owner who cares about the payment, the term and how the obligation appears, and an owner, partner or facilities lead who signs; each needs a different page of the same proposal and raises a different objection. Public and institutional accounts run on rules rather than preferences: informal quote thresholds below which a purchase can proceed, formal sealed-bid or request-for-proposal processes with specification and response requirements, existing cooperative or state contract vehicles that let an entity buy from an already-awarded agreement without a new solicitation, board or council approval calendars, fiscal-year and appropriation boundaries, and vendor registration, insurance or certification prerequisites. Institutional buyers such as school districts, health systems and universities often add their own internal standards. Requirements differ by jurisdiction and entity type and change over time: identify the obligation class that applies, then verify the current rules with the entity's own purchasing office rather than assuming, and never coach a public buyer on how to avoid their own process.

included: role-by-role decision mapping and the objection each role raises
public and institutional buying routes, approval calendars and prerequisite registrations
identifying the obligation class and verifying current rules with the purchasing office
excluded: legal advice on procurement law or on whether a particular route is available to an entity
writing a specification designed to exclude competitors

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an entity's purchasing office confirms thresholds, vehicles or calendars that differ from the recorded route, or a stakeholder change is reported

pros.claim: Knowing the route early determines whether there is a deal at all this fiscal year, which saves months of misdirected effort
pros.example: discovering that a district can buy from an existing cooperative award and does not need a new solicitation, moving the timeline forward by a full budget cycle

pros.claim: Addressing each role's objection in its own language shortens the internal argument the customer has without you
pros.example: a one-page section for the technology owner on scan destinations and device access control alongside the finance summary

cons.claim: Public routes are slow, formal and occasionally decided on price alone, so honest total-cost work can lose to a compliant low bid
cons.example: a well-built proposal beaten by a lower per-page rate that carried a minimum commitment the evaluation did not weigh

cons.claim: Rules vary by entity and change, so any generalisation risks being wrong in a way that costs an award
cons.example: assuming a threshold that applied to a neighbouring city and submitting the wrong document set

failure_modes: selling only to the pain owner and being surprised by finance or technology at the end
assuming a procurement threshold or route instead of confirming it with the purchasing office
helping a buyer split or structure a purchase to avoid their own process
missing a registration, insurance or certification prerequisite and being disqualified on a technicality
acceptance_tests: the file names each decision role, their stated objection and who ultimately signs
for public and institutional buyers the file records the confirmed route, the source of that confirmation, the approval dates and any prerequisite registrations
revisit_triggers: a role changes hands mid-cycle, or a new stakeholder appears late
the entity changes thresholds, adopts or leaves a cooperative vehicle, or moves its board calendar

nodes.definition: Enforce a hard sales-side gate: no device recommendation, no minimum commitment and no page rate leaves the building on the strength of an estimate when evidence exists or can be obtained. Acceptable evidence is a meter reading or usage report from the existing devices, the customer's own supply purchase history, or the incumbent's invoices showing billed pages, captured over a period long enough to expose seasonality rather than a single flattering month. Where evidence genuinely cannot be obtained — a brand-new office, a customer who will not release data, an incumbent who will not produce meters — the proposal states in writing that the configuration and rates rest on a stated assumption, names the assumption and its source, and specifies the true-up mechanism that will correct the commitment after a documented baseline period once real meters exist. This node is the selling-side expression of the no-overselling rule, and it cuts both ways: proposing capacity, device count or a minimum the evidenced volume cannot justify is a failure, and undersizing to win on price is equally a failure, because it produces overage invoices, a device running past its duty capability and a relationship that breaks in month four. Evidence also decides the argument between a customer's belief and the meter: the meter wins, and the difference is shown to the customer rather than hidden.

included: the gate rule, acceptable evidence types and the minimum period they must cover
the labelled-assumption plus true-up fallback where evidence is unobtainable
the symmetry rule that undersizing is as much a failure as oversizing
excluded: how meters are read, how a walkthrough is conducted and the right-sizing arithmetic itself, which belong to the fleet-assessment knowledge base
ongoing meter collection and billing on a live account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-installation meters or first-quarter invoices show volume materially different from the basis the proposal was built on

pros.claim: The gate removes the trade's most common source of customer resentment before it is created, at the cost of one extra week
pros.example: a clinic quoted against twelve months of meters instead of a manager's recollection, whose first invoices arrive as promised

pros.claim: Evidence turns a price argument into a factual conversation the honest vendor tends to win
pros.example: showing that the volume the incumbent bills for does not match the meters on the machines

cons.claim: Insisting on evidence slows the cycle and can lose deals to a competitor happy to quote from a guess
cons.example: a prospect who takes a same-day quote from a rival rather than wait for meter reports to be collected

cons.claim: Evidence periods can mislead when they land entirely inside a seasonal peak or trough
cons.example: meters read across a school district's summer showing a fraction of its academic-year volume

failure_modes: configuring from a single month of data and calling it evidence
accepting a supply history as volume without checking coverage or device count
writing an assumption into a proposal without a true-up mechanism to correct it
quietly undersizing to reach a target payment
acceptance_tests: no configuration, minimum commitment or page rate is issued without either documented volume evidence or a written, labelled assumption with a defined true-up mechanism
the evidence period is stated on the proposal and is long enough to cover the account's known seasonality
where the customer's belief and the evidence differ, both appear in the proposal
revisit_triggers: new meters, invoices or supply history arrive after the proposal is built
a baseline period completes and the true-up mechanism must be applied
an account's workflow change makes the evidence period unrepresentative

nodes.definition: Handle the most abused mechanic in this vertical honestly, deliberately and in writing.
